newsitem.title: GERMANY: German president to send message to Guernica.
newsitem.headline: German president to send message to Guernica.

text.p: Germany's ambassador to Spain will read out a message from President Roman Herzog at a ceremony in Guernica this weekend to mark the 60th anniversary of the city's destruction by German bombers, Herzog's office said on Thursday.

A German newspaper said the president would recognise the "guilt" of German soldiers for the bombing raid on April 26, 1937, carried out to help the nationalist forces of General Francisco Franco in the Spanish Civil War.
A spokesman for the president's office declined to comment on the content of the message.
The raid by bombers of the German Condor Legion inspired Pablo Picasso's anti-war masterpiece "Guernica".

The Frankfurter Rundschau newspaper said in an advance release from Friday's edition that Herzog would apologise to survivors and their relatives. It said the text was intended as a message of "memorial and mourning".

Earlier on Thursday, the German parliament rejected a motion to discuss the bombing raid. Opposition members had wanted parliament to formally express its regret but Chancellor Helmut Kohl's coalition voted against a debate.
